q: Give the definitions of demand as given by famous economists and state the conditions for demand, also?
a: Answers: Definition of Demand: “By demand economists mean an effective desire i.e. the desire which can be satisfied, by virtue of the possession of the means of its satisfaction.” (A.N Agarwala) “The demand for anything at a given price is the amount of it, which will be bought per unit of time at that price.” (Professor Benham) Conditions for Demand: Power to Purchase: The desire or need for a thing cannot be called want or demand in Economics unless we are capable to buy it. E.g. we want to buy a motorcycle but we have no money (Capacity) to purchase it. In this case, it is a desire, not demand; but if we have money to buy it, it can rightly be called demand. Will to Purchase: The will to purchase a thing is as important as the capacity to purchase it. E.g. If we are capable to buy a motorcycle but have no will to own it for any reason; in this case, the desire for a motorcycle cannot be called demand. Demand against Price: Unless we are aware of the market price of a thing, we cannot decide its quantity to be purchased, though we have the capacity and will to purchase it. Actually, the demand is the quantity of a thing, for which the buyer is eager to pay, at a particular price. That is why it is necessary for a buyer to be aware of the price of the goods he demands.

q: Write down the assumptions and factors affecting demand?
a: Answers: Assumptions of Law of Demand: There are certain conditions to prove the accuracy of the Law of Demand, If these conditions are changed, the law will not hold good. These conditions are called "Assumptions" In Economics. They are as under: Similarity of Units: The goods to be sold, under the observation of the law, must be the same in size, shape, weight, taste, quantity, and standard. Changes to income: The incomes of the buyers should remain the same. An increase in income means an increase in purchasing power, which may cause the failure of the law. Change in Tastes: If the taste of buyers is changed, they will not care about spending more money on inferior commodities. The taste of buyers must not be changed. Changes in Fashion: The changes in fashion cause the Law a failure such as the change in taste. Possibility of rising in price in the future: When there is the possibility of rising in price in the future, people will buy more and more quantities, even at a little high price, and thus the law may be upset. Changes in Population: The law fails, down when a rapid rise or fall takes place in the population. The demand increases, even at a higher rate, 10% a particular commodity with the rapid increase in population and it decreases with the sudden fall in population, even at a lower rate. Factors Affecting Demand: Changes in Taste and Fashion: If the taste and fashion of the people change in regard to a particular commodity, its demand increases or decreases accordingly.
